ordered_diagnoses: Epidermoid cyst in the cerebellopontine angle

s1.syndrome_frame: Facial asymmetry with possible cranial nerve involvement in a neonate
salient_findings: Enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal on MRI
Profound hearing loss in the left ear on auditory brainstem response testing
key_facts: 4-week-old male patient
Left facial asymmetry observed during crying
Passed infant hearing screening
MRI showed an enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal
Follow-up MRI showed considerable growth of the mass
Auditory brainstem response testing demonstrated profound hearing loss in the left ear
Histopathological examination revealed a vascular lesion with low levels of mitotic activity
Biphasic lesion composed of vascular nodules among spindle cells
Ki-67 labeling index: 5% to 10%
CD34 and CD31: Positive for endothelial cells

raw.rationale: The histopathological examination revealed a vascular lesion with low levels of mitotic activity, a biphasic lesion composed of vascular nodules among spindle cells, and a glomeruloid-like architecture of vascular epithelial nodules, which are characteristic features of hemangioma. Additionally, the positive staining for CD34 and CD31, which are endothelial cell markers, further supports the diagnosis of hemangioma.

rejected.label: Lymphangioma
rejected.why: Although the pattern is similar to lymphangiomatosis, the presence of vascular nodules and spindle cells, as well as the positive staining for CD34 and CD31, are more characteristic of hemangioma.

rejected.label: Epidermoid cyst
rejected.why: Epidermoid cysts are typically characterized by a cystic structure filled with keratinous material, which is not consistent with the histopathological findings in this case.

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Meningiomas are typically characterized by a higher mitotic activity and a different histological pattern, which is not consistent with the findings in this case.

rejected.label: Epidermoid cyst in the cerebellopontine angle
rejected.why: This option is a more specific location of epidermoid cyst, but the histopathological findings do not support the diagnosis of epidermoid cyst.
